title: align-credential-affinity-and-stream-factory-ergonomics
author: Maya R. Singh
description:
Context and motivation: Customers reported transient 401s and elevated token-exchange load when many short-lived streaming sessions were created concurrently. The root cause was frequent credential rotations and a lack of locality between session consumers and the credential cache. This PR introduces a lightweight SDK-side 'credential affinity' layer plus a unified StreamFactory ergonomics surface across Python/TypeScript/Go to (1) reduce reauth churn for bursty streaming loads, (2) make async iterator / generator cancelation and heartbeat semantics consistent across languages, and (3) harmonize backoff presets and telemetry tags for auth/retry behavior.

Summary of changes: single continuous description of the work —
- SDK surface: add StreamFactory abstraction (create_stream) that returns a typed cancellable stream handle and accepts an optional "affinity_key" to pin a stream to a credential affinity slot. Documented ergonomic patterns for automatic cleanup and explicit close.
- Auth: credential-affinity registry (client-side) with soft pinning and time-based lease backoff to avoid thundering reauths. Adds metrics (sdk.auth.affinity_hits / affinity_misses / affinity_evictions) emitted from all SDKs with consistent tag schema.
- Retries: introduce "adaptive_lease_backoff" preset that is used for streaming sessions by default; aligns backoff windows across languages and adds a small randomized jitter to spread out simultaneous refreshes.
- Telemetry: ensure auth/retry telemetry includes linear ticket id when present and a per-session correlation id so server-side traces can join SDK-initiated refreshes with request flows.
- Tests & CI: cross-sdk integration tests (local harness) to simulate 500 concurrent short streams were added; flaky reauth scenario reproduced and validated.
- Version bumps: python 0.14.0, typescript 2.5.0, go v1.8.0.

Migration notes: By default behavior is backwards compatible; customers who previously relied on per-request credential refresh semantics will see fewer token rotations. To opt out, pass affinity_strategy="none" to client constructors. There is a small behavioral change for users who inspect low-level token rotation events; we recommend using the new telemetry metrics instead.

- [x] integration test harness for simulated concurrency
- [x] docs/upgrade notes updated

Related: references ENG-2048, ENG-2099, SUP-1420 for customer incident and follow-ups.

review_comments: Ethan Brooks (reviewer): Nice design. Two asks: (1) please add a short section in the python doc explaining the eviction policy and how it interacts with the GC; (2) TS linter flagged an unused import in stream/factory.ts.
Maya R. Singh (author): Addressed both — added doc paragraph and fixed the import. Pushed follow-up commit (see commits).

Ines Martinez (reviewer): Can you ensure the affinity metrics include the customer_id tag when available? We need that for QA replay.
Author: Added customer_id as an optional tag; will be omitted when absent (keeps PII controls).

Samuel Kim (reviewer): Go impl looks good; one nit about context cancellation propagation to the credential refresh goroutine.
Author: Updated factory.go to wire parent context into the refresh loop and added a test.
ci_summary: All CI jobs passed on merge: python unit + integration (pytest) ✅, typescript unit + lint + integration (jest + eslint) ✅, go unit + integration (go test) ✅. One flaky TS e2e previously failing on CI but stabilized after increased test harness timeouts — reran and passed.
release_notes: Python SDK 0.14.0: Add StreamFactory and credential affinity; adaptive_lease_backoff preset; telemetry metrics for affinity.
TypeScript SDK 2.5.0: Add StreamFactory and credential affinity; aligned retry presets and tags.
Go SDK v1.8.0: Credential affinity registry and cancellable StreamHandle; improved context cancellation semantics.
Notes: Default behavior is backward-compatible. To disable affinity set affinity_strategy="none".
manual_migration_steps:
- Update to the new SDK versions.
- If you have custom token refresh hooks, validate they interoperate with the affinity registry by running the provided concurrency harness.
- Monitor sdk.auth.affinity_evictions metric during ramp to verify slot sizing.
post_merge_actions:
- Cut release tags for py/ts/go and publish changelogs.
- Coordinate with infra to add new telemetry metrics to the dashboards.
- Watch SUP-1420 for customer follow-ups.
notes_for_release_manager: This changes auth telemetry shape (adds affinity_* metrics and per-session correlation id). Backward compatible but please announce in SDK release notes and notify SRE to update alert queries if they filter on token rotation counts.
qa_summary: Integration harness simulated 500 concurrent short lived streams (5s average) and verified <10% token refresh rate compared to baseline. End-to-end traces show per-session correlation id present and joins with server traces. No regression in streaming latency observed.
example_snippet:
# Python example (affinity)
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=ENV['REDWOOD_KEY'], affinity_strategy='slot')
stream = client.streams.create_stream(model='gpt-xx', affinity_key='user:123')
for chunk in stream:
    if should_cancel():
        stream.cancel()
        break
notes: This PR focuses on client-side affinity and ergonomics. Server-side affinity and token issuance policies are out of scope and will be addressed in a follow-up (ENG-2099).
